turns.text: Hey Lloyd, I finally got my CAD setup sorted. I found this Autodesk-Fusion-360-for-Linux project hosted on GitHub by user cryinkfly. It seems stable enough for my quick sketches.
That's great news, Alan. The cryinkfly repository is indeed a popular choice for getting Fusion 360 running on Linux. Glad to hear it's working for you.
Yeah, it beats dual-booting. By the way, did you see the weather forecast for this weekend? It looks like rain again.
Yes, it looks like another wet weekend. I hope you have some indoor projects planned, like those CAD sketches.
Actually, I was thinking of ordering a new mechanical keyboard if the weather keeps me inside. Do you have any recommendations?
If you're into tactile feedback, the Keychron Q series is usually well-regarded. Would you like me to check current prices?
Maybe later. For now, just keep an eye on that GitHub project updates for me.
Understood. I'll monitor the cryinkfly repository for any significant changes.

Lloyd, I watched a really interesting talk by Cyrus Clarke yesterday. He presented a talk on how AI leaves the screen, enters the real world, and is accepted by people without reading as terrifying. It was quite profound.
That sounds like a compelling perspective. Cyrus Clarke often explores the intersection of physical interaction and digital intelligence. Did he mention specific examples?
He talked about robotic interfaces that feel natural. It made me think about our own interactions. Anyway, I'm trying to decide what to make for dinner tonight.
Given the late hour, maybe something quick? Pasta with a simple tomato basil sauce is always a safe bet.
Good idea. I think I have basil in the fridge. Thanks, Lloyd. Oh, and don't forget to remind me about the hardware order next week.
Noted. I'll set a reminder for next week regarding your hardware order.
Perfect. I'm heading out to buy the basil now. Talk later.
Have a nice trip. I'll be here when you get back.
